summary: This bill aims to enhance the integrity of Medicare hospice care by imposing a 5-year moratorium on new hospice enrollments, increasing oversight and survey frequency for certain programs, prohibiting payment for failure to meet quality data reporting, ensuring independence of physician certifications, allowing additional providers to certify terminal illness, and modifying payment structures for various hospice services.

scores.thoughts: This bill is entirely focused on reforming and ensuring the integrity of hospice care under the Medicare program. It introduces measures like temporary moratoria on new hospice enrollments, enhanced oversight, increased survey frequency, and changes to payment structures and certification processes. These changes aim to improve the quality and accountability of hospice services within the existing public healthcare framework (Medicare), rather than shifting towards private healthcare or expanding public healthcare access broadly. The bill is about refining an existing public healthcare service.

The bill focuses on the Medicare hospice benefit, which is a component of the social safety net providing end-of-life care. By implementing measures to ensure the integrity, accountability, and appropriate payment for hospice services, the bill aims to strengthen the provision of this specific benefit. It is not about expanding or reducing the overall scope of welfare spending, but rather improving the efficiency and quality of an existing social safety net program.
